You need to specify how to connect the products; in other words, use `
` to separate them.
instruction: Enable Windows Sticky Keys and keep them enabled. From the provided Coles catalogue, save every product whose full name contains `Body Wash` and costs less than $9 to `answer.txt` on the Desktop, one exact product name per line in catalogue order.
gt_steps: Keep Sticky Keys enabled throughout the task.
Read the Coles catalogue PDF already open in Chrome.
Find the body wash products and compare their advertised prices.
Identify every product with `Body Wash` in its full product name that costs less than $9.
Identify `Palmolive Naturals Body Wash 1 Litre` priced at $6.50.
Identify `Dove Serum Body Wash 300mL` priced at $7.50.
Identify `Sukin Botanical Body Wash 1 Litre` priced at $8.97.
Identify `Thankyou Body Wash 1 Litre` priced at $8.97.
Identify `Nivea Shower Body Wash 1 Litre` priced at $8.50.
Write each full product name exactly as shown in the PDF, with one product per line.
Do not include prices, products costing exactly $9, or products costing more than $9.
Save the file as `answer.txt` on the Desktop.
Leave the saved file on the Desktop.

result.command: powershell -NoProfile -Command "$flags=[int](Get-ItemPropertyValue -Path 'HKCU:\Control Panel\Accessibility\StickyKeys' -Name 'Flags' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue); if (($flags -band 1) -eq 1) { Write-Output 'STICKY_KEYS_ENABLED' } else { Write-Output 'STICKY_KEYS_DISABLED' }"
